# Meta’s AI agent Muse launches in UK 

 Regulators will be watching the U.K. rollout of Muse carefully. 

![GERMANY-US-TECH-POLITICS-FACEBOOK-META-DISINFORMATION](https://www.politico.eu/cdn-cgi/image/width=1160,height=773,quality=80,onerror=redirect,format=auto/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/23/GettyImages-2192359273-scaled.jpg)

 The Meta logo is seen on a phone in Frankfurt, Germany on Jan. 8, 2025. | Kirill Kudryavtsev/AFP via Getty Images 

 November 24, 2026 7:00 am CET 

 By Mizy Clifton 

LONDON — Meta rolled out its personal AI agent Muse to the U.K. adults on Tuesday, promising users a tool they can trust to lend a “helping hand” on everything from chasing a refund and renewing car insurance to doing the Christmas shopping. 

It is the first AI agent product to be launched by a Big Tech company in the U.K., and regulators will be watching closely. 

The Digital Regulation Cooperation Forum (DRCF), comprising the Competition and Markets Authority, Financial Conduct Authority, Ofcom, and the Information Commission, published a statement last month warning that AI agent products “may amplify and accelerate risks” to consumers.

Reuters reported last week that Meta staffers had raised concerns internally about “undesired actions” carried out by the agent since its debut in the U.S., from accessing encrypted messages to supplying bogus information about purchases (a Meta spokesperson said these were “isolated incidents.”) 

In a blog post published Tuesday morning, Meta sought to reassure would-be users that although the agent is built to carry out tasks on their behalf, Muse is “private, safe and secure by design.” For example, users can choose whether their interactions with the agent are used to develop and improve Meta’s AI — though will need to actively switch this setting off.

“We’ve engaged constructively with the appropriate regulatory authorities and will continue to do so,” Meta said in its blog post.
